Verified the new dimensions and scale factor directly against the shipped code.

v2.72 changes: Three related additions. Grid Truss (in Individual & Grid Cameras): a new Hide Primary Ring cross-bracing while the grid is enabled checkbox suppresses the Primary Ring's interior cross-bracing beams (only while the grid is on — cross-bracing behaves exactly as before with the grid off), and a new Grid truss rails dropdown (Off/Rows/Columns/Both) draws simple rail beams at the grid's own height, positioned exactly on its row/column lines and reaching to the room's edges. Two new 3D camera styles — Slim Style (a genuinely thin/flat body, visually distinct from the cubic PrimeX Style) and Larger Style (the PrimeX Style shape at 3x scale) — taking the total from 3 to 5. Camera 3D style is now independent per system — Primary Camera Ring, Secondary Camera Ring, and Individual & Grid Cameras each have their own style dropdown and remember their own choice (all 19 camera-placement call sites tagged with their system accordingly), rather than one style applying everywhere; Individual & Grid now defaults to Slim Style specifically so it reads as visually distinct from the rings. Hotkey 7 now cycles only the Primary Ring's style, as that's the most frequently used array — clicking a camera directly in the 3D view still cycles a style too, but only for that camera's own system. Along the way, fixed a real pre-existing bug uncovered by this work: the default style index (1) actually resolved to "Box Camera", not "PrimeX Style" as a stale comment claimed — corrected the default to genuinely be PrimeX Style for both rings. All new logic (per-system style resolution and defaults, truss rail row/column math against known grid parameters, all four truss modes, cross-brace suppression across every enabled/checked combination, 1-row/1-col and margin edge cases) verified via isolated testing, since this sandbox has no Three.js rendering access; full syntax check clean throughout.

v2.71 changes: Two real bugs, both found from a screenshot. Grid camera model dropdown was invisible — traced to a stray .camera-preset-dropdown{display:none;} rule in a "legacy/invisible" CSS reset block, which turned out to be hiding all six per-model dropdowns (North/South/East/West/Ring2/Grid), not just the new one — it had apparently gone unnoticed because nobody had needed to change a per-wall camera model recently. Removed just that one rule; the other entries in that block are genuinely intentional (hidden proxy elements) and were left alone. "Individual & Grid Cameras" section title showed the literal text "&amp;" — same root cause as a bug fixed once before for "People & Props": the i18n dictionary value used the &amp; HTML entity, but the i18n code applies it via textContent for any string without real HTML tags, which doesn't decode entities. Fixed the one dictionary entry, then swept every other dictionary string for the same pattern (entity present, no real tag) to make sure nothing else was quietly broken the same way — nothing else was.

v2.70 changes: Camera Grid is now fully live/parametric instead of a one-shot generator — like the Primary/Secondary Ring, it recomputes automatically from inside upAll() whenever you drag a grid control or resize the room, gated by a new Enable camera grid checkbox (default off, matching the Secondary Ring's own enable pattern). Removed the old Generate/Clear buttons since they're no longer needed. Grid cameras are session-tracked separately from hand-placed Individual Cameras, so toggling the grid or dragging its sliders never touches manually placed cameras — verified this holds even through a room resize, and added a defensive reset (grid tracking + enable checkbox) at all five places a saved layout, shared layout, config, or built-in preset can replace the individual-camera list wholesale, so loading one while the grid happens to be left enabled from earlier in the session can no longer add an unwanted extra batch on top of it. Wall margin fixed — the previous clamp could push cameras outside the room entirely once the margin slider exceeded roughly half the room's shorter dimension (x0/x1 were clamped independently against different thresholds, so they could cross or one could run away from the other); margin is now clamped once, symmetrically, per axis, so oversized margins simply collapse the grid smoothly toward the room's centre line/point instead. Individual Cameras and Camera Grid moved into their own new "Individual & Grid Cameras" section, positioned directly below Secondary Camera Ring (previously nested inside Primary Camera Ring) — Camera Grid model selection was already present since v2.69 and needed no change. Updated Help (English and Spanish) to match the new location and live behaviour.

v2.69 changes: New Camera Grid tool (Camera Count panel, below Individual Cameras) — generates an evenly-spaced top-down array of cameras (rows × columns, wall margin, own height slider, any camera model) as ordinary individual cameras, so each one stays fully editable/deletable afterwards. Grid height is deliberately independent of the Primary Camera Ring's Camera height slider, so a perimeter ring and an overhead grid can sit at different heights — built off a real gallery install (perimeter ring + dense top-down grid) where hand-crafting the layout as a one-off JSON import proved too fiddly to edit afterwards. "Clear Last Grid" removes only the most recently generated batch this session. Added matching Help documentation (EN+ES) under Cameras.

v2.68 changes: Corrected the remaining Prime-series ranges — Prime 13W (8m), Prime 17W (14m), and Prime 41 (20m) added using the figures given directly, without applying this file's 30% reduction on top of them a second time (they'd already been reduced before being given). PrimeX 13's default range is now 12m (was briefly 10m last update) — again, the user's own already-cautious figure, used as-is. Verified all four through the real dropdown UI, not just the underlying data: selecting each one now shows exactly 12m/8m/14m/20m on the rendered cameras.

v2.67 changes: Sense-checked the previous update first — confirmed no PrimeX/SlimX/VersaX/Flex figures were disturbed by last update's edits (only PrimeX 13's range was ever touched, exactly as intended). Prime 13 added to the LEGACY group — the 8-bit "Prime" series (distinct from PrimeX) from the same OptiTrack chart. Re-extracted the source PDF directly as a structured table rather than relying on the flowed text, since the raw text had genuinely ambiguous column breaks — this showed clean, unambiguous data for Prime 13 (70°×49° FOV, 12.2m passive-marker range × 0.70 = 9m), but also revealed that Prime 13W and Prime 41 have no range figure in the chart at all, and Prime 17W's cell contains a garbled "15.2m??????" in the source PDF itself — not an extraction artifact. Added only Prime 13 for now rather than guessing numbers for the other three; flagged for follow-up. Point cloud colour override — a "use single colour instead" toggle with a colour picker, for scans with washed-out colour or for a cleaner look in a client-facing capture; switches the material between the scan's own per-point colours and a flat override colour, verified both directions and that toggling off correctly restores the original colours (not just hides the picker). Download GIF for the current view + Animated 2D Coverage — sits right under Animated 2D Coverage in the View menu, matching the existing Orbit/Flythrough/Top-Down/Cable GIF pattern, but deliberately leaves the camera exactly where it is rather than moving to a fixed camera path; verified the camera position is genuinely untouched throughout recording, and that the coverage sweep starts and stops cleanly around it.

v2.66 changes: Legacy OptiTrack cameras added — V120:Duo and V120:Trio (the old 8-bit-sensor cameras from the OptiTrack comparison chart) now sit in their own "LEGACY" group at the bottom of every camera model dropdown, using a real HTML optgroup rather than a fake separator option. Ranges use a 30% safety reduction as requested (8m stated passive-marker range × 0.70 = 5.6m, rounded to 6m) — a slightly larger margin than this file's usual 25%, deliberately kept separate in the code comments so the difference doesn't get lost later. PrimeX 13's default range is now 10m (was 19m) — and this turned out to need fixing in two places, not one: the range slider's own hardcoded default didn't actually match the preset value even before this change (it showed 8m on a fresh page load regardless of what the preset said), so that's corrected too, and now genuinely shows 10m on first load rather than just being correct in the underlying data. While adding the new dropdown entries, audited all six camera-model dropdowns (main plus north/south/east/west/ring2) against each other and found they'd already drifted apart — the four per-wall dropdowns and the secondary-ring one were missing Flir Blackfly S and Vive Basestation, and the main dropdown was separately missing SlimX 13. Fixed all of it so every dropdown now lists exactly the same models. Verified the whole thing through the actual UI flow, not just by reading the option lists: selecting each new camera from the real dropdown correctly pushes its FOV and range through to the rendered cameras, confirmed no duplicate entries ended up anywhere after the fixes, and caught (and corrected) an accidental duplication my own bulk edit introduced in the main dropdown before shipping.

v2.65 changes: LAS file support for Point Cloud Import — both FARO and XGrids recommend exporting scans as .las, so it's now supported directly alongside .ply, dispatched automatically by reading the file's actual signature bytes rather than trusting its extension. LAS is a genuinely different binary format from PLY: coordinates are stored as scaled integers rather than direct floats, and colour (when present at all) sits at a different byte offset depending on which of several point data formats the file uses. Rather than working from the spec by hand, built a real LAS-writing pipeline to generate proper ground-truth test files first, then verified every byte offset against them: a LAS 1.2 file with 16-bit RGB (exact match on both position and colour, point-by-point against known values), and a LAS 1.4 file with no colour that uses the newer 64-bit point count field instead of the legacy 32-bit one (also exact match, and confirmed the point count itself was read from the correct field). Also handles two edge cases found worth guarding for: some LAS writers store 8-bit colour directly in the nominally-16-bit RGB fields without scaling up, which the parser now detects and corrects for automatically rather than rendering everything washed out; and LAZ-compressed files (not currently supported) get a clear message telling you to re-export as uncompressed LAS, rather than failing silently or producing garbage. A 1.5 million point synthetic LAS file confirmed decimation, and the existing scale calibration and Z-up alignment tools were verified to work correctly on LAS-sourced clouds exactly as they already did for PLY, since both formats feed the same underlying point/colour buffers.

v2.64 changes: Point cloud scale calibration — click two points directly on the visible scan (real raycasting against the actual point geometry, not just a flat floor plane, so it works at any height) with a known real-world distance between them, then either Scale Room to Match (the recommended default — a precision instrument like a FARO scanner is genuinely built for accurate real-world measurements, so it's usually the room's own dimensions that need correcting, not the scan) or Scale Cloud to Match for the less common case where the room is the one you trust. Verified the raycasting itself against the real uploaded scan (confirmed the measured distance matches an independent direct raycast at the same screen position), and verified both scaling directions separately with known factors. Import 3D can now rotate on all three axes — added Tilt (X) and Roll (Z) sliders alongside the existing Turn (Y), for models that come in lying on their side or facing the wrong way. Verified the values apply correctly and round-trip properly when deselecting and reselecting an object. Caught and fixed a real mistake made while writing this update's Help documentation — a find-and-replace had duplicated a section title and scrambled the Spanish card order; rebuilt that section cleanly and reverified it matches the English structure.

v2.63 changes: Point Cloud Import — new section at the bottom of the left panel for bringing in a real site scan (laser scan or Gaussian Splat capture, binary .ply) as a visual reference for planning against actual mounting points, an existing ceiling grid, or obstructions. Built as its own dedicated import path rather than extending the existing Import 3D → PLY handling, since that assumes a solid meshed surface and would render a genuine point cloud (which has no faces at all) as nothing. Handles two colour schemes automatically — plain RGB, or Gaussian Splat spherical-harmonics colour, decoded with the standard 3DGS formula. Large scans (tested against a real 3.17 million point, 205MB capture) are automatically decimated to a browser-friendly point budget, reported in the status message. A "Source is Z-up" toggle handles the common case where scan software treats Z as vertical instead of this app's Y-up convention — implemented as a one-off rebuild of the position data rather than a live combined rotation, deliberately avoiding the kind of Euler-order mistake this project has hit before with combined-axis rotations; verified the conversion is exactly mathematically correct and round-trips back to the original coordinates when toggled off. Position/rotation sliders align the cloud with the room without touching the underlying point data, so they stay responsive even at a million points. The cloud is a working reference only: verified it's excluded from GLB exports (checked the actual exported file's node list, not just the code), and it doesn't persist through Save Layout. Tested throughout against the real uploaded scan data, not synthetic files alone — cross-checked the loaded bounding box and colours against an independent analysis of the same file to confirm the parser reads real Gaussian Splat data correctly, not just files shaped like my own test cases.

v2.62 changes: Room size range extended further, down to 0.5m — Ground length and Ground width now go as low as 0.5m; verified the room correctly rebuilds at that size, not just the slider bounds. Version number now shown in the sidebar header, small and subtle next to "Keeler System Designer" — a quick way to confirm a deploy actually went out, without needing to open Help.

v2.61 changes: Room size range extended down to 1m — Ground length and Ground width both now go as low as 1m (was 2m); the top end was already 50m. Verified the room actually rebuilds correctly at both new extremes (1m×1m and 50m×50m), not just that the slider attributes changed. The secondary (mezzanine) floor dimensions already covered 1–60m, so no change was needed there.

v2.60 changes: Fixed the stuck GLB/PDF export pop-up — the status message shown while generating a GLB or Camera Viewports PDF was never actually being removed from the page: the GLB export never removed it at all, in any scenario, and the PDF export only removed it in the success path, leaving it stuck if anything went wrong partway through. Rebuilt both around a shared toast helper: a manual dismiss button (✕) is now always present, so it's never a dead end even if something unexpected happens, and the toast is guaranteed to clear via try/catch/finally covering the entire operation — verified this properly by deliberately breaking the exporter mid-operation and confirming the toast still cleared, not just testing the success path. New File menu, first in the bar as requested (File / View / Assets / Visualise / Export / Hotkeys) — Save Layout, Load Layout, Share to Cloud, and Load from Share Code all moved here from Export. Verified the whole bar's new order directly and confirmed each moved item still works from its new location.

v2.59 changes: Wall Options moved to Assets — Wall Edge Snapping now sits in the Assets menu right alongside Custom Walls and Cut Wall Tool (the existing "show wall" toggle), rather than in Export where it didn't really belong. Fixed a real display bug: "People & Props" and "Labels & Overlays" were showing the literal text "&" instead of an ampersand whenever the language got reapplied — the menu's translation system correctly uses plain text rendering (deliberately, to avoid ever interpreting stray HTML), but the dictionary entries themselves had "&" typed in as literal characters rather than a plain "&", so nothing was there to decode it back. Fixed both entries at the source. Verified both fixes directly: the ampersand renders correctly after switching languages (not just on first load), and Wall Edge Snapping still toggles correctly from its new location.

v2.58 changes: Reports grouped together in Export — Camera Alignment Report moved from Visualise into Export, joining Cable Report and Truss Component Report under a new "Reports" group label, in that order. While restructuring this, found and fixed a pre-existing bug: Truss Component Report was sitting under a "Wall Options" group label that had nothing to do with it, immediately followed by a second, correctly-labelled "Wall Options" section for the actual wall settings — a leftover copy-paste duplicate. Now there's exactly one Wall Options group, and Truss Component Report lives under Reports where it belongs. Verified all three reports still open their correct modal via real clicks after the move.

v2.57 changes: 3D Model Export (GLB) for client proposals — Export → 3D Model (GLB) offers three options (Clean / With Coverage / Full Detail) producing a standard .glb file with no editing access and no pricing/quote data (that never lived in the 3D scene graph to begin with, so there was nothing to strip). A separate standalone page, viewer.html, gives a lightweight orbit/zoom viewer with independent, freely-combinable checkboxes for whichever overlay layers were included in a given export (FOV wireframes, coverage, camera labels, alignment crosshairs, measurement lines) — genuinely independent toggles, not a curated set of fixed presets, since that was the specific requirement. Getting the export itself working took real debugging: the first attempts crashed with a stack overflow inside the export library's own serialization, traced through several rounds of isolation testing (a bare test mesh exported fine, ruling out the library itself; the live scene's camera meshes did not) down to a genuine root cause — some meshes carry a userData.cameraRoot property that's a circular reference back to their own parent object, and it turns out Object3D.clone(true) itself (not just the exporter afterward, as first assumed) does an internal JSON-based deep copy of userData that chokes on that loop. Fixed by stripping userData from the live objects immediately before cloning and restoring it right after, rather than trying to clean the already-broken clone. Verified thoroughly rather than assuming: all five overlay types individually confirmed present/toggleable via real interaction (menu clicks, real mouse drags for measurement points, not just calling functions directly) and inspecting the actual binary .glb output with a glTF parser to confirm the exact node names and structure; the viewer tested loading via URL parameter, via file picker, and correctly showing an empty layer panel when an export has no optional overlays at all. Documented both the export options and the viewer in Help before shipping.

v2.56 changes: Menu cleanup — Camera Viewports PDF and Cable Report both moved to the Export menu. While moving Cable Report, found it was actually already duplicated (a second, independently-wired copy already existed in Export) — removed the Assets-menu one rather than creating a third. Removed decorative emojis from the Assets and Visualise dropdowns (Add Person/TV/Rack, Manual Truss Designer, Camera Alignment Tool, Camera Alignment Report, and the Measure Distance row) — kept the functional ✓ checkmarks that indicate on/off state and the → sub-item indent markers, since those carry real information rather than decoration. Also fixed a genuine bug found along the way: the Measure Distance row's checkmark indicator had a ruler emoji hardcoded in place of the standard ✓, inconsistent with every other toggle row — corrected to match. Verified all moved/edited items still work correctly with real clicks, not just visual inspection: Cable Report still opens its modal, Camera Alignment Tool still toggles, Add Person still spawns a person.

v2.55 changes: Confirmed and completed the two-way link between Camera ID and the on-screen camera labels — setting a Camera ID in the Alignment panel already updated that camera's floating label in the scene, and double-clicking a label in the scene to rename it already synced back to the panel, the report, and the PDF, all from prior work. Rather than assume it worked from reading the code, verified every direction with genuine simulated interactions (not just calling functions directly): typed a Camera ID in the panel and confirmed the actual rendered scene label text changed; double-clicked a real camera label in the 3D view (found via its actual screen projection), typed a new value, pressed Enter, and confirmed the panel field, the underlying data, and a freshly-generated PDF all picked up the change. Along the way, found and fixed one real gap: the label-refresh path swapped in a new texture but discarded the temporary sprite it came from, so a debug property meant to make this testable wasn't actually landing on the live label — fixed so it does. Also found the Spanish Help translation was missing a paragraph the English version already had (documenting the double-click behaviour) — added it, so the two language versions stay in sync. Verified the whole chain again with a full HOLOSYS 8-pod layout.

v2.54 changes: Camera ID & Serial Number — two new fields in the Camera Alignment panel for labelling each camera with your own ID and recording its serial once installed. These persist against each camera's stable auto-label rather than a temporary index, so they survive a full model rebuild, Auto-Optimise, and save/load — verified all three directly rather than assuming. Camera Viewports PDF (Visualise menu) renders an actual snapshot of what each camera sees from its exact position and aim, 4 per page, with ID/serial/model/bearing/tilt alongside each — and each image renders at that specific camera model's real aspect ratio, computed properly from its hfov/vfov (tan(hfov/2)/tan(vfov/2), not a naive ratio of the two angles, which would've been measurably wrong — confirmed the two differ by about 4% for a typical camera). Tested a narrow 47°/27° camera against a very wide 150°/110° one side by side in the same export and confirmed their rendered aspect ratios came out at 1.810 and 2.613 respectively — an exact match to the formula by hand. Verified the full pipeline by opening the actual generated PDF with a PDF-reading library afterward (not just checking that a download happened): correct page count, correct image count, correct text on every camera, and the viewport/camera state fully restored afterward. Also tested with a full HOLOSYS 8-pod layout (32 cameras, truss/drape/LEDs/green floor all on) to confirm everything works together, not just in isolation. Documented both features in Help before shipping.

v2.53 changes: Camera Alignment Tool — a new on-site installation aid, requested after a real install: enable it via Visualise → Camera Alignment Tool, then click any camera to see exactly how to aim the physical hardware to match the design. Shows position, a compass bearing (0°=N, clockwise), and a tilt angle (degrees from horizontal), plus a North offset setting (Display Assets) for calibrating against real/magnetic North on site rather than the app's own virtual North. The bearing/tilt maths were verified against six hand-computed test cases (due N/E/S/W plus tilted up/down) before trusting them on real cameras. A red crosshair plus dashed sightline marks the exact aim point in the 3D view, and its coordinates are given as distance from the West and North walls for physically taping a mark on site. View From This Camera freezes the main viewport at the camera's exact position/aim/FOV as a sanity check — this needed care to get right: the render loop and mouse-drag orbit controls both key off the camera mode, so the preview uses its own distinct mode string rather than reusing an existing one, confirmed by reading both code paths first rather than assuming it'd stay put. Verified this with an exact position/FOV match on entry and an exact restore on exit. A Camera Alignment Report lists every camera's position, bearing, tilt, and aim point for a walkaround printout. Every camera in the app (wall-mounted, individual, HOLOSYS pod cameras) now carries a stable label for this (e.g. "North #2", "Pod 3 — C2") — while wiring that up, found and fixed a real pre-existing bug where camera model names were never actually being recorded (wallPreset()/ring2Preset() silently returned no name field at all). Verified the whole feature end-to-end with genuine simulated mouse clicks (not just calling functions directly), confirmed normal click-to-cycle-style behaviour is unaffected when the tool isn't active, and documented it in Help (Camera Alignment Tool, English and Spanish) — checked this before shipping rather than after, given it was missed for the Volumetric System last time.

v2.52 changes: Volumetric System documented in Help — checked before shipping and found the entire HOLOSYS feature (pod presets, camera layout, circular truss, outriggers, drape, LED panels, green floor) had no Help wiki coverage at all despite everything built over the last several sessions. Added a full new “Volumetric System” section (English and Spanish) covering all of it, positioned in the nav right after Truss & Structure. Verified it actually works, not just that the HTML exists: navigates correctly, all 6 cards render, appears in search results, and translates correctly to Spanish.

v2.51 changes: Helper text expanded across the menu — the small explanatory hints from the Volumetric System section are now used throughout: Visualisation (FOV/truss brightness, coverage height, and all five coverage/wireframe toggles — the most jargon-heavy section in the app), Primary Camera Ring (FOV, range, truss/clamps, auto-optimise), Secondary Camera Ring (what enabling it actually does), Room Design (secondary floor opacity/matching, stairwell direction), and Display Assets (LED wall curve, floor opacity). Focused on controls that aren't self-explanatory from their label alone, rather than adding a hint under every single slider. New global toggle — “Show helper text” checkbox at the top of the panel turns all of this on/off in one click (24 hints currently), for anyone who'd rather have a shorter menu once they know the app. Preference is remembered across sessions. All the existing Volumetric System hints were also brought under this same toggle, so it controls everything consistently rather than just the new additions. Verified the toggle actually hides/shows every hint, that the preference survives a page reload, and that hints translate correctly to Spanish.

v2.51 changes: Explainer hints extended to the rest of the menu — found that a “Show helper text” toggle and the underlying .control-hint infrastructure already existed from earlier work; audited every section against its actual control count and added hints where the label alone genuinely wasn't enough (wall ID colours, wall brightness being render-only, what a Brain Bar is, the scale-reference person, the secondary floor plane's mezzanine use case, truss legs, floorplan aspect-ratio lock) — while deliberately leaving alone sections like Import 3D and Asset Library where the controls (position/rotation/scale) are already self-explanatory, so the toggle stays meaningful rather than every slider getting a hint regardless of whether it needs one. Verified the existing global toggle correctly shows/hides all 31 hints (up from 24) together, and that the new ones translate correctly in Spanish. Removed the emoji from the QUOTE tab on the right edge of the 3D view, since it was obscuring the vertical text.

v2.50 changes: Bottom LED ring dropped another 10cm (to 0.6m) and its upward tilt now mirrors the top ring exactly, rather than both aiming at the same fixed point — the top ring still aims down at a fixed 1.2m reference, but the bottom ring aims up by that same vertical delta from its own (now-lower) height, so the two angles match in magnitude with opposite sign regardless of the bottom ring's exact height. Verified directly against the built geometry rather than trusting the math on paper: bottom ring measured at +18.642°, top ring at −18.642° — an exact mirror. Middle ring is unaffected, still level. Re-checked panel counts and camera clearance for both 8-pod and 12-pod after the height change — still safe in both cases.

v2.49 changes: Correct visual layering — outrigger masts now sit at their own radius, behind the LED panels and in front of the truss legs (confirmed order from centre outward: cameras -> LED panels -> outrigger masts -> truss legs), rather than at the same radius as the LED setback. Verified directly: 4.15m (LED) < 4.35m (mast) < 4.64m (truss leg). Green floor within drape — new checkbox adds a chroma-key green disc matching the drape/truss ring radius, independent of the drape's own colour choice. New “Volumetric System” section — all HOLOSYS controls (presets, truss, drape, LEDs, green floor) moved out of Presets into their own top-level collapsible section, placed directly under Secondary Camera Ring. Verified the DOM order and that every control still works correctly from its new location. LED rings now angle toward a fixed aim point — the bottom ring tilts up and the top ring tilts down, both aiming at a point 1.2m above the floor at the centre; the middle ring stays level. Used lookAt() rather than hand-derived Euler angles this time, and verified it empirically first in isolation before relying on it (confirmed a plain mesh's +Z face points exactly at the target, dot product 1.0) — then verified all three rings on the real panels (dot product 1.0 in every case: bottom and top aiming at 1.2m, middle level). HOLOSYS structural elements recoloured — the circular truss ring, its legs, and the outrigger masts/arms are now a chroma green very slightly lighter than the drape's own green, so they read as part of the same chroma-key environment. Confirmed this only affected the HOLOSYS call site and not the shared truss-building function's other uses — the rectangular truss still renders in its normal colour.

v2.48 changes: Outrigger bars — cameras that sit tangentially offset from their pod (the wide top pair, the extended bottom-right camera) now have visible mounting hardware connecting them back to the pod, instead of floating in space with no visible support: a vertical mast at the pod's true radial line, sized to that pod's tallest camera, with a horizontal arm at each camera's own height reaching out to its exact position. Verified this rigorously given past mistakes with rotation math on this project — checked each arm's actual rendered endpoints (not just its reported position/length), confirming one end sits exactly on the mast and the other exactly on the camera, for all four camera types per pod. Bottom-right camera (C4) moved another 30cm — confirmed still too close even after the previous 50cm adjustment, now 80cm total extra (85cm full offset from the pod centreline). This is now the single largest camera deviation in the rig (exceeding the 80cm top-pair spread), so the drape/truss ring-sizing formula was updated to consider it too — verified the safety margin still holds at exactly 0.20m. Verified outriggers build with zero leak across repeated preset loads and clear correctly when switching to an unrelated preset.

v2.47 changes: Reverted the circular truss changes from v2.46 — back to the polygon-approximated ring (straight chord segments) and the matching chord-based cutting-list report format, per request. Verified the reverted report text matches the v2.45 format exactly. HOLOSYS camera heights adjusted: top tier (overhead cameras) raised 10cm to 3.00m, second-highest tier (the standard upper pair) lowered 10cm to 2.10m — both confirmed directly. Re-verified the drape/truss safety margin still holds (unaffected by pure height changes, since the worst-case tangential-offset sizing depends on horizontal spacing, not vertical position) — still exactly 0.20m clearance.

v2.46 changes: Overhead camera row raised another 10cm (back to 3.00m) for a bit more clearance above the top LED panel, per direct confirmation. Circular truss is now actually circular — replaced the octagon/dodecagon polygon approximation with a true continuous ring (a real curved torus, not straight chord segments), verified the rendered geometry directly rather than assuming (radius matches the computed value exactly, to the sixth decimal place). Legs are unchanged — still straight vertical tube, since only the ring itself needed to become a true curve. Truss report now lists the ring as bespoke radius elements instead of pretending it's cuttable from straight stock — since a genuine curve can't be decomposed into a standard cutting list the way a straight chord could, each pod-to-pod arc is now reported with its radius, arc angle, and arc length, flagged clearly as a custom-fabricated part to confirm with your truss supplier. The connector section was updated to match — legs still get a spigot/bracket entry, but the old "ring joint between segments" line no longer applies now that there's no joint between adjacent bays. Verified the whole HOLOSYS system still works together correctly with these changes — LED panels still clear every camera, drape still builds correctly per bay, and the report generates cleanly for both 8-pod and 12-pod.

v2.45 changes: Two more HOLOSYS spacing corrections, both confirmed directly: the overhead camera row (previously 3.00m) is now at 2.90m — its mounting clamp was clipping the top LED light panel (2.60m) — and the bottom camera pair (C3/C4) gets an additional 0.5m on the "right" camera (C4), on every pod, standard or overhead, since the existing spacing was still too tight. With this extra room the bottom pair now clears the collision-avoidance threshold on its own (0.6m apart before any automatic nudging is even needed), so that system no longer has anything to do for this pair — verified directly (0 cameras flagged as adjusted, down from 12 previously). Re-checked everything downstream that depends on these numbers: drape/truss ring sizing is unaffected (the 80cm standard-pod top-pair spacing is still the larger, dominant case), LED panels still safely clear every camera position, and the Truss Component Report still generates correctly with the circular truss included.

v2.44 changes: Fixed a real regression — the 80cm wide-offset camera fix from last time had silently failed to persist into the shipped file (confirmed and re-verified: pod 1's C1/C2 were back to the old ~10cm spacing instead of the confirmed 1.6m). Re-applied it properly this time and triple-checked it's actually in the file before shipping — verified again with the same precision as before (8 cameras extended for 8-pod, 12 for 12-pod, exact 1.6m separation, correct drape/truss ring sizing). Apologies for the wasted round-trip on that one. HOLOSYS circular truss now included in the Truss Component Report — when the “Include circular truss” checkbox is on, its ring segments and pod legs are automatically folded into the same Bill of Materials as the rectangular truss, including their own cutting-list breakdown and a dedicated connector estimate (the ring's joints aren't the standard 90°, so this is flagged clearly rather than presented as a specific Milos part number). Also fixed two related gaps found while wiring this up: the report previously always said “Truss not shown” if the rectangular truss checkbox was off, even with the circular truss on with real data to report; and separately, the connector section would still show rectangular-truss corner/T-junction estimates even when no rectangular truss existed at all. Verified all three states — circular only, rectangular only, and both together — report correctly in each case.

v2.43 changes: Pleated drape — new “Pleat density” slider (0 = flat panel, higher = more folds per metre of width) for both the rectangular Drape Rail and the HOLOSYS circular drape, building a real folded-fabric mesh (a proper zigzag geometry, not a texture trick) rather than a flat plane. Verified the geometry directly: flat stays an ordinary 4-vertex plane exactly as before, pleated produces the exact expected vertex count for its width and density, folds are symmetric (alternating in and out, matching how real curtains actually pleat), and repeated rebuilds (e.g. dragging the slider) don't leak into the scene's occlusion tracking. HOLOSYS camera layout corrected again — re-examined page 6 with a working image viewer this time and can now say with certainty it's a wiring/port-mapping diagram (acquisition unit → camera port assignments), not a spatial layout — it doesn't encode camera extension distances at all, confirmed by direct inspection rather than pixel-guessing. The actual layout came from direct confirmation: on standard pods only (not the overhead ones), the top camera pair (C1+C2) sit ~80cm apart tangentially toward their neighbouring pods for a wider vantage angle, while C3/C4 and all overhead-pod cameras are unchanged. The drape/truss ring sizing was updated to match this new, larger worst-case camera spread — verified the exact expected radius (√(4.00²+0.80²)=4.079m) and a safe 0.20m clearance margin for both 8-pod (8 cameras extended) and 12-pod (12 extended), with no new collision risk introduced.

v2.42 changes: LED panels now actually face the capture-volume centre — the previous orientation formula looked plausible but had a sign error in the underlying rotation math (worked through by hand this time, then verified against the real rendered transform: the world-space face normal now dots to exactly 1.0 against the direction to centre, for every panel checked, at every pod angle — not just assumed correct). Camera collision-avoidance updated — threshold changed to 0.4m and the nudge to 0.1m, per request. Since the 0.1m nudge is smaller than the gap needed to clear a 0.4m threshold from the 0.1m starting separation, the check now runs iteratively (repeating until every pair actually clears 0.4m, rather than a single pass that could’ve left pairs only partway there). The drape/truss ring-sizing math was updated to match — it depends on how far collision-avoidance can push a camera, and that number changed along with the new parameters; both now reference the same named constants so they can’t silently drift apart the way a hardcoded number could. Verified for both 8-pod (12 cameras adjusted) and 12-pod (18 adjusted) with the drape safety margin landing at exactly the intended 0.20m clearance in both cases.

v2.41 changes: HOLOSYS LED light panels — new “Include LED light panels” option in the Volumetric section, 3 panels per pod matching the reference photo (confirmed via pixel-cluster analysis of the bright panel regions, since visual inspection wasn’t available this session — the photo consistently shows 3 panels per pod column at 3 similar height bands). Panels sit at a slightly larger radius than the camera ring itself, i.e. physically behind every camera relative to the capture-volume centre, so a camera looking inward is always looking away from its own pod’s panels — verified directly rather than assumed (panel radius 4.15m vs. worst-case camera radius 4.04m, confirmed for both 8-pod and 12-pod). A “Lights: On/Off” button toggles a warm-white lit look vs. a dark unlit-fixture look on the existing panels (visual only, not an actual scene light source — flagged clearly in the UI). Verified panel counts (24 for 8-pod, 36 for 12-pod), zero leak into the scene’s occlusion list across repeated rebuilds, and clean clearing when switching to an unrelated preset.

v2.40 changes: PA Stand added to the Asset Library — 6th item alongside Tripod, Speaker, Microphone, Flight Case, and Director Chair: a wide folding tripod base, telescoping pole, and speaker-mount cup at the top (no speaker cabinet, since stands are positioned/sold separately from the speaker that sits on them). Built with the same corrected leg-pivot technique from the recent Tripod fix, verified the same way — all 3 legs land at exactly 0°/120°/240° at identical radius. Click to place, drag/rotate/scale/delete, and save/load all worked immediately with zero special-casing, since the underlying library system was already generic.

v2.39 changes: HOLOSYS drape now correctly encloses the cameras — previously sized off the pod-base ring (Dp), which actually put the drape *inside* the camera positions, meaning the cameras themselves could poke past the backdrop. Found a second, subtler issue while fixing this: a flat-sided ring’s panels bow inward relative to its own corners (the “apothem” effect), so sizing off the vertex radius alone wasn’t enough either — the ring is now sized so its panel midpoints, not just its corners, clear every camera with margin, verified for both 8-pod and 12-pod. Camera collision avoidance — any two HOLOSYS cameras closer than 0.3m are now automatically separated by nudging one an extra 0.5m apart (reported in the load toast); re-examined page 6 of the install manual via direct text/OCR extraction to confirm it’s a wiring/numbering diagram rather than a precision spec, so this rule is what actually guarantees clearance now. Fixed three real geometry bugs, found and verified through direct coordinate math rather than visual inspection: tripod legs were all landing in the same spot regardless of their intended 120°-apart angles (a THREE.js Euler rotation-order quirk — a leg hanging straight down the local Y-axis is unmoved by a Y-axis spin applied before the outward tilt, so needed an explicit rotation order to fix); the person model’s arm rotation direction was backwards, making shoulders flare outward and hands tuck in rather than a natural hang; and the microphone’s boom and capsule were built independently and had drifted apart, now sharing one pivot so they can’t misalign. Screengrab split into two options in the Export menu — “Screengrab” (no annotations) and “Screengrab + Dims” (the previous behaviour, floor/height dimension lines included) — the keyboard shortcut (Ctrl+S) is unchanged and still includes dimensions.

v2.38 changes: Drape Rail — new controls in Studio Walls for soft-goods drape hanging from the perimeter truss, full height down to the floor. Each side (N/S/E/W) toggles independently so you can leave a gap for an entrance, with a black or chroma-green material choice. HOLOSYS circular truss + drape — the previously-deferred circular truss is back, now specifically to support hanging a chroma-green (or black) backdrop right at the pod ring itself. New controls in the Volumetric (HOLOSYS) section: include the ring truss (with a leg at each pod position), include the drape, an adjustable truss height, and the same colour choice. Truss height is explicitly flagged as a placement aid rather than vendor spec, with a reminder to stay clear of the ~3m overhead cameras and under your real ceiling height. Both new drape systems reuse the same self-cleaning occluder pattern already fixed for the LED wall/brain bar — verified safe against repeated rebuilds (e.g. dragging the truss-height slider) with zero leak into the scene's occlusion list, and correctly clear when switching to an unrelated preset.

v2.37 changes: Asset Library — new section in the left panel for placing common studio items that aren't cameras/people/TVs/racks: Tripod, Speaker, Microphone, Flight Case, and Director Chair. Click to place (spawns at room centre), then drag in the 3D view to position — matching how People/TVs/Racks already work. Right-click or Shift-click a placed asset to select it, then use the Selected Asset panel to rotate (slider or ← → keys) and scale (0.3x–3x), or Delete/Backspace to remove it. Fully wired into Save/Load Layout (round-trip verified) and cleared correctly when a Quick Start preset loads (HOLOSYS presets deliberately leave existing assets in place, since you might want furniture already placed in the volume before adding a pod ring). These are simple procedural placeholder models, not real product geometry — if real STL/OBJ files are available for any of these, Import 3D already supports bringing those in directly with exact geometry.

v2.36 changes: HOLOSYS preset corrections — pods are not all identical, per page 6 of the 4DViews manual: the camera arrangement actually cycles every 4 pods, with pods at cycle positions 2 and 4 (e.g. POD-2, POD-4, POD-6...) carrying an additional overhead camera on a raised arm (confirmed ~3.0m) for full head/top-down coverage, alongside the standard upper and floor-level pairs every pod has. That cycling pattern (repeated twice for 8-pod, three times for 12-pod) now generates correctly — 4 overhead cameras for 8-pod, 6 for 12-pod, verified pod-by-pod. Room-fit check corrected — now gates on 4DViews’ own published minimum (9m x 9m floor, accounting for structural rigs and safety clearance beyond the bare ring), rather than a smaller size derived only from the ring’s own footprint, which would have let through rooms too small in practice. The on-screen toast also now flags the published 4m minimum ceiling height as a reminder — the app has no ceiling-height concept to check this automatically, since rooms are only modelled by floor length and width.

v2.35 changes: HOLOSYS volumetric presets (8-Pod / 12-Pod) — new “Volumetric (HOLOSYS)” section in Presets generates the exact 4DViews HOLOSYS pod ring geometry from their Studio Guidelines: 8 pods at 45° spacing or 12 pods at 30°, camera radius Dc=4.00m, pod-base radius Dp=3.73m, each pod carrying its real 4 FLIR Blackfly S cameras (top pair + bottom pair, all aimed at the capture-volume centre). Unlike the other Quick Start presets, this one does not set room dimensions — it centres the ring in whatever room you already have configured and refuses with a clear on-screen warning (exact required size vs. current size) if the room is too small, since the point is to check whether a given space can fit the 8-pod or 12-pod layout. Bottom camera height (0.10m) was confirmed against the real rig; top camera height (2.20m) is an estimate from the reference photo, not a number in the manual, and is flagged as such in the on-screen toast. A ring truss for mounting lights/mics above the pods was intentionally left out of this pass (the real hardware is freestanding pods, not a connected truss) — flagged as a possible future addition to the Manual Truss Designer rather than bundled into this preset.

v2.34 changes: Remaining collapsed left-panel sections translated — Presets (Quick Start preset buttons, saved-preset cards, Save/Load/Rename/Delete actions and their confirmation dialogs), Import Floorplan, and Import 3D now all follow the active language, completing coverage of all 9 collapsible sections in the System Designer panel. Saved presets and their buttons now also re-translate live if you switch language while looking at them, matching the same fix already applied to saved quotes. Fixed a formatting bug found while translating — one description (the floorplan intro, in both languages) contained a bolded phrase that was rendering as literal <strong> tags instead of bold text once the language-switching code touched it. The translation mechanism now detects real markup in dictionary text and renders it properly instead of escaping it.

v2.33 changes: Click-and-drag for walls, LED wall & brain bar — matching the existing TV/Person dragging, you can now left-click and drag custom walls, the LED wall, and the brain bar directly in the 3D view instead of only using sliders. Dragging a wall perpendicular to its own length also drags any wall connected at that corner (same behaviour as the existing arrow-key move, just continuous); dragging along its own length moves only that wall. Right-click / Shift-click still selects a wall for keyboard rotation as before. Fixed a related bug found while building this: the LED wall and brain bar rebuild functions were pushing fresh occluder references into the scene's occlusion list on every call without ever removing their own previous entries — harmless when rebuilding once per slider change, but would have silently leaked hundreds of stale references during a real click-drag (which fires many rebuilds per second). Both now clean up their own entries first, and dragging them updates the 3D view live without forcing a full scene recalculation on every mouse move, matching the light-weight feel of TV/Person dragging.

v2.32 changes: Hotkeys modal translated — the Keyboard Shortcuts panel (title, tabs, hints, all 29 reserved/built-in action labels, custom-action UI) now follows the active language, and correctly re-translates if you switch language while the modal is already open rather than only on next open.

v2.31 changes: Menu bar dropdowns fully translated — all four top-bar menus (Assets, Visualise, View, Export) now switch to Spanish under ES: every group label, checkbox item, and action (around 70 items in total — Camera FOV, Coverage Overlay, Optimisation tools, Truss Builder, Viewport Angle buttons, Animation modes, Export/Collaborate options, etc.). v2.30 changes: Quote panel tab button fixed — the vertical “QUOTE” tab on the right edge had a fixed height that clipped the longer Spanish “PRESUPUESTO”; it now grows to fit whichever language is active. Send to Pipedrive panel translated — the whole panel (search box, all five action buttons including Attach Proposal PDF, status messages) now follows the active language — it was entirely English before regardless of the language toggle. v2.29 changes: Full Spanish translation of the System Designer panels — every label, checkbox, slider, and section inside Room Design, Studio Walls, Primary/Secondary Camera Ring, Visualisation, and Display Assets now switches to Spanish under ES (previously only the section headers were translated, leaving all the expanded content in English). v2.24 changes: Back to a single self-contained HTML file — the v2.21 split into products.js/styles.css/js/*.js was purely a maintainability change and turned out to be fragile to deploy (missing one sibling file silently breaks the whole app, which is exactly what happened). v2.18 changes: Interactive tour bugfix — the tour's highlights (Presets, Room Design, Camera Count, Visualise menu, etc.) all live inside the System Designer panel, which is hidden while the Help tab is active. v2.16 changes: Secondary ring coverage fix — previously, enabling the secondary camera ring alone was enough to split coverage/aim optimisation into ground + secondary zones, even with "Show floor plane" unticked. v2.14 changes: Ground Supports bugfix — connecting a Run from a Primary/Secondary truss node to a Floor anchor (or vice versa) wasn't registering because node hit-testing only checked where the click ray crossed the current Freeform working-height plane, missing nodes sitting at a different height. Node picking now uses the actual on-screen position of each node, so clicking a truss node or a floor anchor selects it correctly regardless of height, and the live preview line snaps to the real node you're about to connect to.

v2.13 changes: Floor Select / Volume Select split — Volume Select is now its own menu tool (4 · Volume Select Tool) instead of a toggle hidden inside Floor Select, so the two read as clearly separate tools. v2.12 changes: Ground Supports — while Freeform is on, the Run tool now connects nodes across the Primary and Secondary truss layers, and down to floor anchor points (new Floor quick-set button jumps the working height straight to 0.00m). These render as dashed purple links with their own count in the HUD, bake into the model on Apply to Model regardless of which ring you applied, and have a dedicated Clear Ground Supports button so you can wipe them without touching either ring's truss layout. Lets you build custom-angled ground support trusses instead of only straight-down legs.

v2.11 changes: Close (✕) buttons — the Manual Truss Designer, Floor Select Tool, and Measure Tool HUDs all have a ✕ in the corner now, so you can dismiss them directly instead of going back to the menu. v2.10 changes: Wipe-to-shorten Erase — the Erase tool now works like an eraser on open-ended runs: click near the tip and drag inward to progressively shorten it, right down to nothing. Legs and junctions (where other runs share the same joint) still delete in a single click, since there's no single "end" to shorten there.

v2.9 changes: Freeform 3D point placement — the Manual Truss Designer has a "Freeform" toggle. Turn it on and a height (Y) stepper appears — set the working height with the −/+ buttons or PageUp/PageDown, then place points as usual; each new point uses that height instead of the fixed ring height, so runs can slope between different levels. Turn Freeform off to go back to placing points on the flat ring plane. Applies to both the live preview and the final "Apply to Model" render, including junction connectors and legs. This completes the planned truss-designer overhaul (ring editing, Import Auto Truss, freeform placement, volume-select aiming).

v2.8 changes: Volume Select — the Floor Select Tool now has a "Volume" toggle. Turn it on and set a height range (metres above the floor), and each selected footprint cell becomes a translucent 3D box instead of a flat tile. Aim to Selection then samples the bottom, middle, and top of each box, so cameras are aimed to cover a full 3D volume — a stage riser, a raised platform, a rig at height — not just the floor. Works on both the ground and secondary floor layers, independently. Freeform 3D point placement (side/perspective view truss editing) is next.

v2.7 changes: Primary/Secondary ring editing — the Manual Truss Designer now has a RING toggle (Primary / Secondary) in the HUD. Each ring keeps its own independent set of runs, legs, and applied/override state, so you can design the primary ceiling truss and the secondary ring's truss separately without them interfering with each other. The height field, grid, and Import Auto Truss all switch to match whichever ring is selected. Next up: freeform 3D point placement (side/perspective views) and a volume-select tool for the "aim cameras" workflow.

v2.6 changes: Import Auto Truss — Manual Truss Designer now has an "Import Auto Truss" button that copies the current auto-generated truss (runs + legs) in as an editable manual layout — a quick, editable starting point instead of building from scratch. Cameras

Camera Models

Select your camera model from the Assets → Camera Model dropdown. This sets the HFOV, VFOV, and range for all wall cameras at once.

  • Prime X series — PrimeX 13, 13W, 22, 41, 41W, 120, 120W, 260, 260W — high-accuracy OptiTrack studio cameras
  • Slim X series — SlimX 13, 22, 41, 120, 260 — low-profile form factor for ceiling or wall mounting
  • Versa X series — VersaX 22, 22W, 41, 41N, 41W, 120N, 120W — outdoor-rated IP66 cameras
  • Flex — Flex 13 and Flex 3 — compact entry-level cameras for small volumes
  • Prime Colour — Prime Colour 12 and 6.8 — colour-passthrough cameras
  • Vive Basestation — HTC SteamVR base stations with 150×110° FOV
  • Flir Blackfly S — markerless Captury system cameras
  • SlamTec Aurora S — an AI spatial-perception / vSLAM sensor, not a mocap camera: an all-in-one dense depth camera with an optional 2D LiDAR. Coverage uses the 120° horizontal depth FOV (the practical sensing cone, narrower than the 180° binocular fisheye tracking cameras), and a 15m range — a conservative figure versus the rated 40m at 70% reflectivity. Pricing shown is a placeholder; verify current SlamTec pricing before quoting.

Tracking bars (DUO3, TRIO3, Mini-Duo 13) are available in the catalogue for quoting but aren't part of the Camera Model dropdown, since they're fixed-baseline stereo units rather than individually-aimed wall cameras.

You can set a different camera model per wall using the per-wall dropdowns in the Camera Count section — useful for mixed setups.

Camera Count & Placement

Under Camera Count in the left panel, set the number of cameras per wall:

  • North wall (front, Z=0) · South wall (back) · East wall (right) · West wall (left)
  • Cameras are evenly spaced along each wall at the set camera height
  • Camera height is set with the Camera height (m) slider — supports up to 10m for high-ceiling rigs

Secondary Camera Ring

Enable a second ring of cameras at a different height — ideal for Performance Capture setups with both high and low cameras.

  • Tick Enable secondary camera ring in the Secondary Camera Ring section
  • Set the Ring 2 camera height independently (e.g. 1.4m for low cameras)
  • Set camera counts per wall for the second ring separately
  • Choose a different camera model for ring 2 (e.g. PrimeX 13W wide-angle for low ring)
  • Show truss for secondary ring — toggle the truss independently from the main ring truss
  • Enable Floor Plane ("Show floor plane") to add a second floor surface at ring 2 height for multi-floor layouts. This is what actually splits ring 2 into its own independent coverage/aim zone — with it off, ring 2's cameras simply contribute to primary floor coverage alongside the main ring, even though the ring itself is enabled.
  • Use the Floor plane opacity slider (below Floor plane height) to control its transparency

Individual Cameras

Place cameras at exact custom positions, independent of wall counts. Found in its own Individual & Grid Cameras section, below Secondary Camera Ring:

  • Tick Show individual cameras
  • Click + Add Camera to place a camera
  • Each camera gets its own model, FOV, and range settings
  • Drag cameras in the 3D view to reposition them

Truss Type

Choose which truss profile the app draws and reports. There are two places, and they always stay in step:

  • Primary Camera Ring → Show truss → Truss type (under the Show truss tick box)
  • Manual Truss Designer → GAUGE dropdown in the designer toolbar (Visualise → Manual Truss Designer). It lists Default (original profile), the Global Truss types F14 / F24 / F34, and the Milos gauges M222–M760. Picking Default or a Global Truss type sets the Truss type above; picking a Milos gauge sets it back to Standard, since Milos trusses use the standard piece lengths

Available types — drawn for the ring truss and grid rails:

  • Standard box truss — the original heavy box profile, unchanged and still the default. Pieces: 250 mm – 4 m (the report and the 3D colour-coding now use the same list, including 1.5 m)
  • Global Truss F14 — compact, TÜV-approved, 100 × 100 mm. Pieces: 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0 m
  • Global Truss F24 — 220 mm series (mobile DJ, shop fitting, small stands), 220 × 220 mm, 35 mm main tubes. Pieces: 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 4.0 m
  • Global Truss F34 — the industry-standard 290 mm series (medium-duty lighting and stage rigs), 290 × 290 mm, 50 mm main tubes (2 mm wall). Pieces: 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 5.0 m
  • Global Truss F22 / F32 — 2-point ladder, 220 / 290 mm, drawn as two chords one above the other with rungs and zig-zag diagonals (the usual orientation for a hung span). Pieces as F24 / F34
  • Global Truss F23 / F33 — 3-point triangle, 220 / 290 mm sides, drawn apex-down (two chords on top, one underneath) and laced on all three faces. Pieces as F24 / F34
  • Global Truss F31 — single 50 mm tube (pipe), no lacing. Pieces as F34
  • Ladder, triangle and single-tube types change the spans only; legs and the designer's corner connectors are still drawn as square boxes of the same size. A Milos gauge picked in the designer is always a box

Good to know

  • The overall external sizes (100 / 220 / 290 mm) and, for F24 and F34, the main tube sizes come from Global Truss's specifications. The diagonal (web) tube sizes are assumed — 8 mm for F14, 16 mm for F24, 20 mm for F34 (and F14's 20 mm main tubes are assumed too) — so the overall size is right but the lattice thickness is a visual estimate. The values are in TRUSS_TYPES in the code if you have the datasheets
  • Piece lengths follow the type in both the Truss Component Report and the colour-coded 3D segments (the colour-code legend and the report's "Standard lengths" line list the selected type's lengths). Spans on the Global Truss types are split to leave the fewest custom cuts first, then the fewest pieces, preferring larger pieces (F14: 0.6 m is 400 + 200 rather than 500 + a 100 mm cut; F34: 11 m is 5 + 5 + 1 m). Anything that can't be made from stock is reported as one custom cut, so a span that isn't a multiple of the type's smallest piece needs one
  • Grid rails normally default to a half-size lattice; for the Global Truss types that setting draws the real size, because half of a real truss size isn't a product. Dims and rail positions are unaffected — they are measured to the truss centreline
  • The setting is saved with the layout; older layouts load as Standard. There is no truss pricing — the product list has no truss items

Camera Grid

An evenly-spaced top-down array — useful for gallery/tracking-volume style installs that combine a perimeter ring with a dense overhead grid. Found in the Individual & Grid Cameras section, below Secondary Camera Ring.

  • Tick Enable camera grid to turn it on — like the rings, it's parametric: it updates live as you drag Rows, Columns, Grid height, Wall margin, or change the camera model, and also repositions automatically if you resize the room
  • Layout by → Total camera count lets you simply type how many grid cameras you want (e.g. 110) instead of setting rows and columns. It tries every row count, picks the one whose spacing along the room and across it is closest to equal, and spaces the cameras evenly edge-to-edge between the wall margins. If the number doesn't divide into a clean rectangle (say 97), some rows get one extra camera, so those rows are spaced a touch tighter and columns stagger slightly rather than leaving a gap. The Rows and Columns sliders then show the result and are greyed out, and a preview line under them gives the actual spacing in metres. Up to 1000 cameras. Column rails and Dims use the rows/columns shown, so with a staggered layout the column rails won't line up exactly with every camera — row rails always do
  • Grid height (m) is independent of either ring's own Camera height slider, so a ring and the grid can sit at different heights (e.g. a wall-mounted perimeter ring at 3m with an overhead grid truss at 5m)
  • Wall margin (m) sets how far the grid is inset from the room edges
  • Choose the grid camera model — defaults to SlimX 13, a common top-down choice
  • Because the grid fully regenerates on every change, it isn't meant for one-off per-camera hand-tweaking — use Individual Cameras above for that. Untick Enable to remove the grid entirely; manually placed individual cameras are never affected
  • For the perimeter ring itself, use the standard North/South/East/West camera counts in the Primary Camera Ring section — keeping ring and grid as separate tools makes each one easy to re-tune independently

Grid Truss (below the grid controls, same section):

  • Hide Primary Ring cross-bracing while the grid is enabled — the Primary Ring's own interior cross-bracing beams can look redundant or visually clash once the grid is doing that job instead; this checkbox only has an effect while the grid is on, so cross-bracing always shows normally with the grid off
  • Grid truss rails (Off / Rows / Columns / Both) draws beams positioned above the grid's camera height — matching how the Primary Ring's own truss sits above its cameras, rather than at the same height — exactly along its row and/or column lines, reaching all the way to the room's edges so they visually connect to the perimeter — independent of, and in addition to, the Primary/Secondary Ring's own truss
  • Rail size (Full truss / Half-size truss / Simple rail) controls how chunky those beams look — defaults to Half-size, since a dense grid with many rails can look cluttered at full truss scale

3D Camera Style

Controls what a camera looks like in the 3D view — purely visual, with no effect on FOV, range, or exports. Each of the three camera systems has its own independent style, since real hardware often differs between them (e.g. Prime-series on the perimeter ring, Slim-series overhead):

  • Five styles: Sphere, Box Camera, PrimeX Style, Slim Style (thin in depth toward the lens with a roughly square face, matching real SlimX-series proportions, so it reads as visually different from PrimeX's cubic body at a glance), and Larger Style (the PrimeX shape scaled up, easy to spot from across the room)
  • Each of Primary Camera Ring, Secondary Camera Ring, and Individual & Grid Cameras has its own style dropdown in its section — Primary and Secondary default to PrimeX Style, Individual & Grid defaults to Slim Style
  • Hotkey 7 cycles the Primary Ring's style specifically, since that's the most frequently used array — it doesn't touch Secondary Ring or Individual & Grid
  • Clicking directly on a camera in the 3D view also cycles a style, but only for that camera's own system — click a grid camera and only the grid's style changes

FOV & Range

Fine-tune field of view and range under Camera Count:

  • H FOV — horizontal field of view in degrees
  • V FOV — vertical field of view in degrees
  • Range (m) — maximum reliable tracking distance (75% of OptiTrack spec by default)
  • Selecting a camera preset from the dropdown auto-fills these values
Cámaras

Modelos de Cámara

Elige tu modelo de cámara en el desplegable Recursos → Modelo de Cámara. Esto ajusta el FOV horizontal, el FOV vertical y el alcance de todas las cámaras de pared a la vez.

  • Serie Prime X — PrimeX 13, 13W, 22, 41, 41W, 120, 120W, 260, 260W — cámaras de estudio OptiTrack de alta precisión
  • Serie Slim X — SlimX 13, 22, 41, 120, 260 — formato de bajo perfil para montaje en techo o pared
  • Serie Versa X — VersaX 22, 22W, 41, 41N, 41W, 120N, 120W — cámaras con protección IP66 para exteriores
  • Flex — Flex 13 y Flex 3 — cámaras compactas de gama de entrada para volúmenes pequeños
  • Prime Colour — Prime Colour 12 y 6.8 — cámaras de paso de color (colour-passthrough)
  • Vive Basestation — estaciones base HTC SteamVR con FOV de 150×110°
  • Flir Blackfly S — cámaras del sistema sin marcadores Captury
  • SlamTec Aurora S — un sensor de percepción espacial por IA / vSLAM, no una cámara de mocap: una cámara de profundidad todo en uno con LiDAR 2D opcional. La cobertura usa el FOV horizontal de profundidad de 120° (el cono de detección práctico, más estrecho que el de las cámaras de seguimiento binoculares ojo de pez de 180°), y un alcance de 15 m — una cifra conservadora frente a los 40 m nominales al 70% de reflectividad. El precio mostrado es provisional; verifica el precio actual de SlamTec antes de presupuestar.

Las barras de seguimiento (DUO3, TRIO3, Mini-Duo 13) están disponibles en el catálogo para presupuestar, pero no forman parte del desplegable de Modelo de Cámara, ya que son unidades estéreo de línea base fija en lugar de cámaras de pared apuntadas individualmente.

Puedes definir un modelo de cámara distinto por pared usando los desplegables individuales en la sección Recuento de Cámaras — útil para configuraciones mixtas.

Recuento y Colocación de Cámaras

En Recuento de Cámaras, en el panel izquierdo, define el número de cámaras por pared:

  • Pared Norte (frontal, Z=0) · Pared Sur (trasera) · Pared Este (derecha) · Pared Oeste (izquierda)
  • Las cámaras se distribuyen uniformemente a lo largo de cada pared, a la altura de cámara definida
  • La altura de cámara se ajusta con el deslizador Altura de cámara (m) — admite hasta 10 m para montajes con techos altos

Anillo de Cámaras Secundario

Activa un segundo anillo de cámaras a una altura distinta — ideal para configuraciones de Performance Capture con cámaras altas y bajas a la vez.

  • Marca Activar anillo de cámaras secundario en la sección Anillo de Cámaras Secundario
  • Ajusta la Altura de cámara del anillo 2 de forma independiente (p. ej. 1,4 m para cámaras bajas)
  • Define el número de cámaras por pared del segundo anillo de forma independiente
  • Elige un modelo de cámara distinto para el anillo 2 (p. ej. PrimeX 13W gran angular para el anillo bajo)
  • Mostrar estructura para el anillo secundario — activa la estructura de forma independiente de la del anillo principal
  • Activa el Plano de Suelo ("Mostrar plano de suelo") para añadir una segunda superficie de suelo a la altura del anillo 2, para diseños multi-planta. Esto es lo que realmente separa el anillo 2 en su propia zona de cobertura/apuntado independiente — sin él, las cámaras del anillo 2 simplemente contribuyen a la cobertura del suelo principal junto con el anillo principal, aunque el anillo en sí esté activado.
  • Usa el deslizador Opacidad del plano de suelo (debajo de la altura del plano de suelo) para controlar su transparencia

Cámaras Individuales

Coloca cámaras en posiciones exactas y personalizadas, independientes del recuento por pared. Se encuentra en su propia sección Cámaras Individuales y de Cuadrícula, debajo de Anillo de Cámaras Secundario:

  • Marca Mostrar cámaras individuales
  • Haz clic en + Añadir Cámara para colocar una cámara
  • Cada cámara tiene su propio modelo, FOV y ajustes de alcance
  • Arrastra las cámaras en la vista 3D para reposicionarlas

Cuadrícula de Cámaras

Una matriz cenital uniformemente espaciada — útil para instalaciones tipo galería/volumen de seguimiento que combinan un anillo perimetral con una cuadrícula cenital densa. Se encuentra en la sección Cámaras Individuales y de Cuadrícula, debajo de Anillo de Cámaras Secundario.

  • Marca Activar cuadrícula de cámaras para activarla — como los anillos, es paramétrica: se actualiza en vivo al mover Filas, Columnas, Altura de cuadrícula, Margen de pared, o al cambiar el modelo de cámara, y también se reposiciona automáticamente si redimensionas la sala
  • La Altura de cuadrícula (m) es independiente del deslizador de Altura de cámara propio de cada anillo, por lo que un anillo y la cuadrícula pueden situarse a alturas distintas (p. ej. un anillo perimetral montado en pared a 3 m con una cuadrícula cenital en estructura a 5 m)
  • El Margen de pared (m) define cuánto se separa la cuadrícula de los bordes de la sala
  • Elige el modelo de cámara de cuadrícula — por defecto SlimX 13, una opción habitual para vista cenital
  • Como la cuadrícula se regenera por completo con cada cambio, no está pensada para ajustes manuales de una sola cámara — usa Cámaras Individuales de arriba para eso. Desmarca Activar para eliminar la cuadrícula por completo; las cámaras individuales colocadas a mano nunca se ven afectadas
  • Para el propio anillo perimetral, usa los recuentos estándar de Norte/Sur/Este/Oeste en la sección Anillo de Cámaras Primario — mantener el anillo y la cuadrícula como herramientas separadas facilita ajustar cada uno de forma independiente

Armadura de Cuadrícula (debajo de los controles de la cuadrícula, misma sección):

  • Ocultar el arriostramiento cruzado del Anillo Primario mientras la cuadrícula está activa — el arriostramiento cruzado interior propio del Anillo Primario puede resultar redundante o visualmente conflictivo una vez que la cuadrícula cumple esa función; esta casilla solo tiene efecto mientras la cuadrícula está activa, así que el arriostramiento se muestra con normalidad cuando la cuadrícula está desactivada
  • Carriles de armadura de cuadrícula (Desactivado / Filas / Columnas / Ambos) dibuja vigas posicionadas por encima de la altura de cámara de la cuadrícula — igual que la armadura propia del Anillo Primario se sitúa por encima de sus cámaras, en lugar de a la misma altura — exactamente sobre sus líneas de fila y/o columna, llegando hasta los bordes de la sala para conectar visualmente con el perímetro — independientes de, y además de, la armadura propia del Anillo Primario/Secundario
  • Tamaño de carril (Armadura completa / Armadura a media escala / Carril simple) controla el grosor visual de esas vigas — por defecto usa media escala, ya que una cuadrícula densa con muchos carriles puede verse recargada a escala completa

Estilo 3D de Cámara

Controla el aspecto de una cámara en la vista 3D — puramente visual, sin efecto en el FOV, el alcance o las exportaciones. Cada uno de los tres sistemas de cámara tiene su propio estilo independiente, ya que el hardware real a menudo difiere entre ellos (p. ej. serie Prime en el anillo perimetral, serie Slim en la cuadrícula cenital):

  • Cinco estilos: Sphere, Box Camera, PrimeX Style, Slim Style (delgado en profundidad hacia el objetivo, con una cara aproximadamente cuadrada, igual que las proporciones reales de la serie SlimX, para leerse visualmente distinto del cuerpo cúbico de PrimeX a simple vista) y Larger Style (la forma PrimeX a mayor escala, fácil de detectar desde el otro lado de la sala)
  • Cada uno de Anillo de Cámaras Primario, Anillo de Cámaras Secundario y Cámaras Individuales y de Cuadrícula tiene su propio desplegable de estilo en su sección — Primario y Secundario usan PrimeX Style por defecto, Individuales y de Cuadrícula usa Slim Style por defecto
  • La tecla rápida 7 cicla el estilo del Anillo Primario específicamente, al ser la matriz más usada — no afecta al Anillo Secundario ni a Individuales y de Cuadrícula
  • Hacer clic directamente en una cámara en la vista 3D también cicla un estilo, pero solo para el sistema propio de esa cámara — haz clic en una cámara de la cuadrícula y solo cambiará el estilo de la cuadrícula

FOV y Alcance

Ajusta con precisión el campo de visión y el alcance en Recuento de Cámaras:

  • FOV H — campo de visión horizontal en grados
  • FOV V — campo de visión vertical en grados
  • Alcance (m) — distancia de seguimiento fiable máxima (75% de la especificación de OptiTrack por defecto)
  • Seleccionar un preajuste de cámara en el desplegable rellena automáticamente estos valores
Tripod Layout Designer & Volume Planner

Tripod Layout Designer

For offsite shoots rigged on 3.2 m tripod PA stands instead of truss. In the Tripod Layout Designer section, tick Rig on tripod stands.

  • The Room Design floor (length × width) is the capture area. Stands go evenly in a ring round it, Distance outside the capture area away (default 1 m)
  • Stands, Cameras per stand (default 2) and the top and lowest camera heights (default 3.2 m and 2.0 m; cameras are spread evenly between). Choose the camera model on the stands
  • Switching tripods on turns the Primary Ring cameras and the truss off; switching it off puts them back as they were
  • Drag a stand in the 3D view to move it; its cameras and cables follow when you let go. Reset stand positions and aims puts them back in the ring
  • Cables run down each stand and across the floor to the switch or rack, so cable lengths reflect floor runs
  • Stand cameras count as cameras everywhere: coverage views, Auto Optimise, reports, cable lengths and the generated quote (one clamp per camera, plus a Tripod PA stand line per stand; set its SKU and price in Quote Builder)
  • Saved with the layout, including moved stands and planner aims. Presets and layouts saved before v2.104.0 aren't on tripods

What stand cameras work with

Stand cameras are ordinary cameras to the rest of System Designer, so these all include them:

  • FOV wireframes and Clip FOV, 2D and 3D coverage
  • Auto Optimise, Aim to Centre, Floor Select and Volume Select (Aim to Selection), whether or not Show individual cameras is ticked
  • Camera labels, cables and the cable report, network switches and the PoE summary, the generated quote, the Pipedrive kit list, and Save / Share

What doesn't apply to them:

  • Primary Ring controls (cameras per wall, camera height, per-wall models): the stands have their own count, heights and model in the Tripod Layout Designer
  • Truss tools (truss designer, grid truss, truss legs): stands replace the truss. Truss Auto Switch is built for truss rigs, so place switches by hand for stands
  • Stands are on the ground floor: they ring the Room Design floor, not the Secondary Floor Plane (the Secondary Ring can still be used alongside)
  • Individual camera editing: stand cameras don't appear in the Individual Cameras list (an edit there would be lost when the stands regenerate). Move a stand by dragging it, and aim with the tools above

Volume Planner

For when you know the volume you need, e.g. a director wants 12 × 12 × 4 m. Open it with Plan a capture volume… (Tripod Layout Designer section, or the top of Room Design).

  • Enter the volume's length, width and height, the rigging (Tripod stands or Truss ring, with their heights and distance outside the volume), and tick the camera models you have
  • For each model it finds the fewest cameras so that the required coverage (default 95%) of points through the whole volume are seen by 3 or more cameras (2 or 4 also available), with every camera aimed by an optimiser
  • It allows for the performer's own body: a point only counts when a marker there facing any way (front, back, left or right) is seen by enough cameras on the side it faces. That's why it asks for more cameras than a simple field-of-view count
  • Results are listed fewest cameras first, with the coverage reached and the weakest height band. If a model can't reach the target with the chosen rigging, its best result is shown
  • Apply sets the design to that layout. Tripods: the room becomes the volume and the stands, model, heights and the planner's aims are set. Truss: the room becomes the volume plus the margin, with the truss height, cameras per wall, model and the planner's aims (shown as Auto Optimise ON)
  • Not modelled: props or other people blocking views, or marker size beyond each camera's range figure (75% of OptiTrack's quoted range). Treat the counts as a starting point and check the 3D coverage view
Trípodes y planificador de volumen

Trípodes

Para rodajes fuera del estudio con soportes PA de 3,2 m. En la sección Trípodes, marca Montaje en trípodes. El suelo de Diseño de sala es el área de captura; los trípodes van en anillo a su alrededor. Elige número de trípodes, cámaras por trípode, alturas y modelo. Al activarlo se apagan el anillo principal y el truss. Arrastra un trípode para moverlo. Los cables van por el suelo y suben por cada trípode, y las cámaras cuentan en cobertura, Auto Optimizar, informes y presupuesto.

Planificador de volumen
